# Aggregate Conveying Line: Start/Stop and Protection Narrative

## 1. Scope and equipment

Material flows in this order: **Hopper / VF-1 → CV-1 → CV-2 → CR-1 → CV-3 → stockpile.**

| Tag | Device | Protective inputs |
|---|---|---|
| VF-1 | Vibratory feeder | Interlocked to CV-1 |
| CV-1, CV-2, CV-3 | Belt conveyors | Zero-speed switch (ZSS), belt misalignment alarm and trip switches (MAS/MTS), pull-cord switches (PCS), plugged-chute switch (PCH) |
| CR-1 | Jaw crusher | Motor current CT (FLC 210 A), lube oil pressure switch (LPS) |

All setpoints and timers below are proposed starting values. Confirm them at commissioning.

## 2. General principles

1. **Start against the flow, stop with the flow.** The line starts from the discharge end back to the feed end, so nothing feeds a stationary machine. It stops from the feed end forward, so every belt and the crusher run out empty.
2. **Trips propagate upstream.** A fault stops the faulted device and everything upstream of it immediately. Equipment downstream runs out in a controlled sequence (Section 5).
3. **Fail-safe wiring.** All protective switches are normally-closed (healthy = closed) and the CT is a 4-20 mA signal. Wire break, power loss, or signal below 3.5 mA is treated as a trip.
4. **Hardwired safety.** Pull-cords and any E-stops are hardwired into the motor starter control circuits, independent of the PLC. The PLC monitors them for indication and for restart logic.
5. **Latched trips.** Every trip latches and shows first-out indication on the HMI. The operator must clear the cause and acknowledge before a restart is allowed.
6. **Control point.** The line is started and stopped only from the control room HMI, in Auto mode. Local/maintenance mode is outside this narrative.

## 3. Start permissives

The HMI Start command is accepted only when all of these are true:

- No active trips, and all pull-cord switches are reset (healthy).
- All misalignment trip switches are healthy and all plugged-chute switches are clear.
- CR-1 lube oil pressure is proven (see 4.3 if the pump is on a separate starter).
- All drives are available (no starter fault or lockout, selected to Auto).
- The audible/visual warning device is healthy.
- The line is in the stopped state. No stop sequence is in progress.

Any trip or missing permissive blocks the start and the HMI shows the reason.

## 4. Normal start sequence

### 4.1 Warning

On Start, the horn and beacon run for **10 s**. No conveyor, crusher, or feeder moves during this time.

- If a permissive is lost or the operator cancels during the warning, the sequence aborts and nothing starts.
- The warning is repeated in full on every start or restart, including after a trip.

### 4.2 Sequence

Each step starts only when the previous step is proven running. A step that fails proving trips the sequence (Section 6).

| Step | Action | Proven when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start **CV-3** | ZSS shows motion within 10 s |
| 2 | Start **CR-1** | LPS healthy and current falls below the idle threshold (4.3) |
| 3 | Start **CV-2** | ZSS shows motion within 10 s |
| 4 | Start **CV-1** | ZSS shows motion within 10 s |
| 5 | Start **VF-1** | Feeder running. The line is now "Running" |

A short step delay (about 5 s) separates steps to limit simultaneous inrush.

### 4.3 Crusher start specifics

- **Lube oil.** Pressure must be proven before the start command. If the pump starts with CR-1, start the pump first and allow up to 30 s for pressure to build. Pressure not proven in that time means a start failure and no crusher start.
- **Current during start.** CT readings are ignored during inrush (first 15 s).
- **Run-up proving.** Current must fall below about 70% of FLC (about 147 A, set from the measured no-load current) within 30 s. Otherwise CR-1 trips as a failed start, because it is jammed or loaded.
- **Starting with material in the chamber.** Never start CR-1 with material in the chamber unless there is no alternative (see Section 7).

## 5. Normal stop sequence (controlled run-out)

A Stop command from the HMI starts a staged shutdown in flow order. This clears material from each machine before it stops.

| Step | Action | Timer before the next step |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Stop **VF-1** immediately | CV-1 run-out time |
| 2 | Stop **CV-1** | CV-2 run-out time |
| 3 | Stop **CV-2** | Crusher clearing time (about 30 s) |
| 4 | Stop **CR-1** | CV-3 run-out time |
| 5 | Stop **CV-3** | Line "Stopped" |

- Run-out timers are set per conveyor from the typical 20-45 s range. Measure them at commissioning with a loaded belt and add a margin of about 10%.
- Overall stop time is about 2.5-3.5 min.
- **Warning on stop.** The 10 s warning is not required for stopping.
- **Faults during run-out.** A pull-cord, trip-stage misalignment, or plugged-chute fault during run-out stops the affected equipment and everything upstream immediately. Remaining downstream equipment continues its timed run-out.
- **Abort.** Pressing Stop does not abort a restart that has already begun its warning. Stop cancels the start sequence and returns to the stopped state.

## 6. Protection and trip actions

### 6.1 Per-conveyor protections (CV-1, CV-2, CV-3)

| Protection | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **Zero-speed switch** | No motion proven within 10 s of start, or speed lost for more than 5 s while running (slip, broken drive, jam) | Trip. Stop the conveyor and everything upstream immediately |
| **Misalignment, alarm stage** | Switch operated for more than 3 s | HMI alarm only, no stop. Flag for operator attention |
| **Misalignment, trip stage** | Switch operated for more than 3 s | Trip. Stop the conveyor and everything upstream immediately |
| **Pull-cord** | Any cord operated | Hardwired stop of that conveyor and everything upstream. Latched until the cord is reset locally. Reset is then acknowledged at the HMI |
| **Plugged chute** | Switch active for more than 3 s at the conveyor's discharge | Trip. Stop the conveyor and everything upstream immediately |

The 3 s delays on misalignment and plugged-chute switches reject momentary surges. The pull-cord stop is instantaneous and never delayed.

### 6.2 Crusher protections (CR-1)

| Protection | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **High current, alarm** | Above 105% FLC (about 220 A) for 10 s | HMI alarm, no stop |
| **High current, feed cutback** | Above 110% FLC (about 231 A) for 10 s | Stop VF-1 until current recovers below 100%, to relieve the crusher. Optional if the chamber is clearing |
| **High current, trip** | Above 120% FLC (about 252 A) for 10 s | Trip. Stop CV-2, CV-1 and VF-1 immediately. CR-1 stops. CV-3 runs out |
| **Failed run-up** | Current above idle threshold 30 s after start | Trip as above |
| **Lube oil pressure low** | LPS not healthy for more than 5 s while running (inrush/start bypass 30 s) | Trip as above, and block restart until pressure is restored |
| **CT signal fault** | Below 3.5 mA | Trip as above |

Instantaneous short-circuit and thermal overload protection stay in the motor starter or protection relay, independent of this logic.

### 6.3 Where plugged-chute trips land

| Switch location | Meaning | Trips |
|---|---|---|
| CV-1 discharge | CV-1 backed up at CV-2 | CV-1, VF-1 |
| CV-2 discharge | Crusher feed chute blocked | CV-2, CV-1, VF-1 |
| CV-3 discharge | Stockpile or chute full | CV-3, CR-1, CV-2, CV-1, VF-1 |

### 6.4 Trip response summary

| Fault origin | Stops immediately | Controlled run-out |
|---|---|---|
| CV-1 | VF-1, CV-1 | CV-2, CR-1, CV-3 |
| CV-2 | VF-1, CV-1, CV-2 | CR-1, CV-3 |
| CR-1 | VF-1, CV-1, CV-2, CR-1 | CV-3 |
| CV-3 | Entire line | None |

The run-out sequence uses the same timers as a normal stop, started from the moment of the trip.

## 7. Restart after a trip

1. Make the area safe, find the cause, and clear it. This includes clearing blocked chutes, resetting pull-cords locally, and realigning belts.
2. Acknowledge the alarm at the HMI. The trip resets only if the initiating condition has cleared.
3. Check that CR-1 and the belts are clear before restarting. If the line tripped while loaded, the crusher chamber and belts may need to be cleared manually. Restarting a jaw crusher full of material risks a failed run-up.
4. Restart as a full start sequence from Section 4, including the 10 s warning.

## 8. Items to confirm

- Whether pull-cords should stop only the affected conveyor plus upstream (as written) or the whole line. This depends on the site risk assessment.
- Whether a lube pump has its own starter and what its pressure build time is.
- Whether the site has E-stops, local isolators, or any HMI-loss behaviour (the line should trip, or run out in a controlled way, on PLC or HMI comms failure).
- Measured run-out times, crusher idle current, and current setpoints.
- Whether the warning must also pulse between start steps, since steps are about 5 s apart.
